posts.cooked:
I wanted to get this topic rolling early this year for one very important reason.

The Gencon housing lottery begins Monday, February 12th. I heard through the grapevine that if you want to get in, you must do so today. I just wanted to throw it out there to get in front of as many people as possible. I’m helpful like that. However, I’ve never had to do this before, so please don’t ask me details (in fact I’d be delighted if someone would walk me through the process and answer any questions I have.)

The not-so-emergency part of this post is: Who’s going? Who’s doing awesome stuff? Who’s not doing awesome stuff but would like to meet up and get some awesome stuff done?

Let’s talk about GenCon!

posts.cooked:
The strictly-about-me part: I’m about to buy badges for the first time in what 15 years? 20? I’m not sure, but I’m super excited!

I haven’t been to GenCon since its last year in Milwaukee, so I’m not registering for any events. Just keeping myself wide open. I’ll also have my 11 year old son along, who may be small but has been the huuugest Sentinels fan for… I don’t know, ever… so we’ll be doing as much Sentinels stuff as possible.

Tips and advice welcome.

And I’d definitely enjoy putting faces to (forum) names if anyone wants to get together and play a game or seven.

posts.name: Paul
posts.cooked:
@deddragon

It is awesome that you are going to Gen Con! The last time you were at Gen Con, I was part of the group that won the costume contest :)

Greater Than Games will have a huge presence at the show this year. In addition to our booth, we've had a dedicated demo room in the concourse outside of the main expo hall for the past two years. This year, our room will be in a better / easier to find location right in the middle of the concourse across from the escalators (for those of you super familiar with the ICC). We'll also have a big banner this year hanging from the ceiling of the concourse outside of our room!

In addition to short demos in our booth, and long demos in our room, we'll be doing a bunch of Sentinel Comics RPG demos in other spaces at the show, and be running a number of panels on board gaming.

I hope to see you there!

I'll be there! In past years, I've volunteered for Greater than Games, which has been great: running demos of their games is basically my favorite thing, and gives me a place to hang out when the crowds get to be too much.

I live in Bloomington (1 hour away in good traffic), but I'll still be entering the housing lottery. (This means I'm buying a convention pass, with the expectation of getting it refunded later, since GtG has in past years given out convention passes.)
